Lithium Battery Charging Guide

Lithium-ion cells should be charged to 4.2 volts per cell using a constant-current constant-voltage profile. Charging above 45 degrees Celsius accelerates capacity loss and can be unsafe, so a quality charger tapers the current near the end of the cycle.

A typical 18650 cell holds about 3000 mAh and delivers 3.7 volts nominal. Discharging below 2.5 volts per cell causes irreversible damage, which is why protection circuits cut the load at a safe threshold.

For long-term storage, keep cells at roughly 40 percent state of charge in a cool place; storing a fully charged pack at high temperature is the fastest way to lose capacity.
